image_tool: Add lsb_factory payload when creating RMA shims. 1. Store the content of lsb-factory to payload when creating RMA shims. Legacy shims don't have lsb_factory payload, so we also need to add it when creating a universal shim. 2. Make `edit_lsb` subcommand modify lsb_factory payload. 3. deprecate `USE_CROS_PAYLOAD` flag, which is not used since CL:518606. BUG=chromium:952733 TEST=make test; manually merge legacy shim and check that lsb_factory is added. factory_install: Patch lsb-factory at beginning of factory installer. In the future, lsb-factory is stored in cros_payload, so we need to use it to patch the actual lsb-factory in stateful partition at the beginning of factory installer. We cannot simply delete the original lsb-factory, because initramfs also adds some parameters into the file which are used in factory installer. BUG=chromium:952733 TEST=manually test on DUT; check that lsb-factory is updated by payload. image_tool: Add UserInput class to unify user input functions. There are some places that require user input to confirm or select options, such as `edit_lsb` command to manually set configs. These blocks have similar behavior and error handling logics. This CL adds a class to unify the input methods, message displaying and error handling. Supported input method includes: - Select from several options - Choose Yes/No - Input a number - Input a string BUG=chromium:944394 TEST=make test Change-Id: Id6fbb1b9ed27cffd6b5e0429bb4196de9abde3fb Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1575181 Commit-Ready: Cheng-Han Yang <chenghan@chromium.org> Tested-by: Cheng-Han Yang <chenghan@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Hung-Te Lin <hungte@chromium.org>

The led behavior define as following: 1. Charging led: led on with charging port active, other port is off. Charging: Amber. Discharging: Off. Power led: System is S0: White System is suspend/S0ix: Blinking white (1 sec on, 1 sec off) System is S5: Off BUG=b:126460269 BRANCH=none TEST=Make sure led behavior intended. CRAS: iodev - Move set node attr functions to iodev_list In order to have cleaner multi-thread access to variables on a cras_iodev. In future commits, setting node attributes could require sending message to audio thread if device is in open. This change is a preparation for that, it moves node attr setter functions to iodev_list module where it has access to audio_thread. BUG=chromium:946356 TEST=unittest Change-Id: I4b48bef3cc96832f9e47772a320f6dbe14840ac4 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1433427 Commit-Ready: Hsinyu Chao <hychao@chromium.org> Tested-by: Hsinyu Chao <hychao@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Cheng-Yi Chiang <cychiang@chromium.org>

CRAS: audio_thread - Use dev_idx to send message from main thread We want to restrict access to iodev and its member variables by only one, main or audio, thread. That means in future sending message between threads can not use iodev pointer as key. This change modifies the audio thread message APIs to use dev_idx instead of iodev pointer. BUG=chromium:946356 TEST=unittest Change-Id: Ibb48be29d2d8e274b1d75d9879964b62d41b7b4a Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1517348 Commit-Ready: Hsinyu Chao <hychao@chromium.org> Tested-by: Hsinyu Chao <hychao@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Cheng-Yi Chiang <cychiang@chromium.org>

Add a unittest to check config skew, old and new. Add a config_skew_unittest as the starting point for defining tests that check for config skew from the old legacy config to the new config approach. The first test is a simple test that checks that the list of postsubmit build targets between master-postsubmit of old config and postsubmit-orchestrator of new config matches. This test is in a failure state right now as master-postsubmit has many more build targets. The test is by default skipped, in the same fashion that the --network tests work. That is they only run if invoked with: ./run_tests.sh --config_skew TEST=./run_tests.sh TEST=./run_tests.sh --config_skew (fails as expected) BUG=chromium:923000 Change-Id: Id64a96164a5bc8eacc61a8a8d3c47a43063ce2ed Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1574479 Commit-Ready: David Burger <dburger@chromium.org> Tested-by: David Burger <dburger@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Andrew Lamb <andrewlamb@chromium.org>
